description:
One return attributed to one planting. The mirror of Block Cost Entry and it exists for the same reason: the ledger records that a settlement paid $84,000, and nothing in the ledger records that four blocks grew the fruit it paid for.

ATTRIBUTION IS THE WHOLE JOB, AND IT IS USUALLY AN ALLOCATION. A packing house settles on a pool, not a block — one statement covers everything delivered in a period, and splitting it back to the blocks that grew it is done on delivered weight, which this app can compute from the Scale Tickets that already carry a field and a block. The BASIS is on the record because it is a judgement: allocating by weight is right for a single variety and wrong the moment two blocks of different grades were pooled, and a farm reading its per-block returns three years later needs to know which was done.

DIRECT IS STILL THE BEST ANSWER WHERE IT EXISTS. A bin sold off one block at a farm stand is Direct at 100 percent, and no allocation improves on that. The allocation machinery is for the pooled case, which is most of the crop on most farms.

THIS IS NOT THE LEDGER, exactly as Block Cost Entry is not. A revenue figure summed from here is an ATTRIBUTION of revenue the ledger already recognised, and the two answer different questions — 'what did the business earn' and 'which ground earned it'. A summary that presented this as the first would be wrong in a way an accountant would catch and a grower would not.

fields.description: The crop year this return is for, which is very often NOT the year it was paid. A settlement on stored fruit lands in the following March, and a register that filed it by payment date would show a barren year followed by a miraculous one.
